prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics and Fluid-mechanical Machines and Systems

learning_outcomes.text: To know, understand and distinguish the different types of maintenance in the industrial field.
To understand the mechanism of failures and determine the useful life of devices.
To know, understand and apply the different mechanical verification techniques, both direct and indirect, fundamentally highlighting vibration analysis.
To apply maintenance to various mechanisms (gears, flexible transmissions, bearings,...).

teaching_methods: Classroom Practices (Problem solving and case analysis)

Laboratory Practices (Practical aspects of maintenance techniques, planning, and management; identification of failure mechanisms; description and use of condition-based maintenance techniques such as Thermography, Vibrations, Ultrasound, Magnetic Particles, and Penetrant Liquids; company visits; specialist conference)
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum score of 40% (2.8 out of 7 points) is required on the final theoretical-practical exam to pass; otherwise, the recorded grade will be 4.9. Attendance at laboratory practices is mandatory for evaluation. For extraordinary calls, differentiated evaluation, and Erasmus students, assessment consists of a final exam covering theory and classroom practices (90%) and laboratory practices (10%). In all calls, a minimum of 5 points out of 10 is required to pass the course.
